candidates.title: I diffed 7 public LeRobot datasets across versions — one silently recalibrated two robot joints
candidates.summary:
I built robot-data-diff (episode-aware diffs for LeRobot datasets) and turned it on public data: 9 revision pairs across 7 popular datasets — v2→v3 migrations and fix commits. Here’s what came out:

A popular dataset silently recalibrated two joints. All 50 episodes of svla_so100_pickplace changed between v2.1 and v3.0 — two action dimensions got mirrored and shifted 90°. Their commit message admits it after the fact (“Fix SO-arm joint frame”), but nothing in the data warns you. candidates.title: Running coding agents on tracker tickets (Jira-like workflows): which models work best?
candidates.summary:
I’m testing how to add AI agents to Jira-like workflows. The agent reads a ticket, edits the repo, runs the tests and reports back. Each ticket runs in its own git worktree so parallel runs don’t collide. I’m using Sharkly.ai for the orchestration.

Questions for the community:

  • Which open models handle the “read ticket → small, scoped code change” loop reliably?
  • Has anyone evaluated agents on real issue-tracker tasks rather than benchmarks?

I’d love to hear about any datasets or eval setups for this.

candidates.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
candidates.summary: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings.
